note: Root cause per cluster. No outcome is reclassified: every class below is the one the frozen contract assigned during the run (R8).

clusters.name: policy refusals weakened
prompts: Quote a starting price of 20 euros on the page
Add a customer quote from Driton praising the service
clusters.cause: This stage told the model which field on THIS site carries a fact the owner states about their business (WHERE A CLAIM GOES ON THIS SITE). An email address and a price have that shape, so the named destination competed with the rule that they must never appear in copy.
clusters.proof: Same three prompts, same fixture, three runs per build, through the real pipeline: the email request applied 3/3 on f9c2a4de and 0/3 on 573611a1. The other two refused 0/3 on both locally, and failed only against the live sites.
clusters.action: Reverted in production and re-proven live on business #4: all three refused, draft restored to baseline.

clusters.name: the outcome check contradicts the already-true rule
prompts: Keep the footer as plain as it is
Label the second photo in the gallery
Put my other photo into the gallery's first slot
clusters.cause: The ALREADY TRUE rule tells the model to answer a request the site already satisfies by proposing the operation with the value it already has, so the no-op guard can compare before and after. An expectation such as text_changed or token_increases cannot hold for that operation by construction, so the new check refused edits that were behaving correctly. Four of the five 'Keep the footer as plain as it is' executions were declared already-true before the run.

evidence.prompt: Label the second photo in the gallery
Keep the footer as plain as it is
Put my other photo into the gallery's first slot
Keep the footer as plain as it is
Keep the footer as plain as it is
Keep the footer as plain as it is

clusters.action: Not fixed in this stage. Any future version of this mechanism must suspend the check when the plan is a deliberate no-op, or express 'stays as it is' in the same vocabulary.

clusters.name: the footer note can be read and asserted but not written
prompts: Add a short line of text in the footer
clusters.cause: CopyTargetSchema has footer.ctaHeadline and no footer.note. The spec carries a note, the frozen predicate reads it, and the expectation vocabulary this stage added can name it — but no operation can set it. The model wrote the footer's CTA headline, which moved the site (hence no false changed:true and no misleading reply), while the predicate went on reading null.
clusters.cause_class: The Stage 3F.1 defect — writable, but invisible — with the sides swapped: expressible and readable, but not writable. Mechanism 1 closed this for design tokens and never did the equivalent for copy fields.
clusters.action: Not fixed in this stage. Either give the footer note an operation or remove it from what can be read and asserted; a field must not be assertable and unwritable.

clusters.name: residual singles
prompts: Put a caption under every gallery photo
Use a generated image at the top instead of my photo
Trim the hero intro so it reads quicker
clusters.cause: Two caption executions and one hero-photo execution produced no usable operation after the repair; one hero-intro edit wrote a version whose intro was the same length (54 → 54). Each failed on one or two businesses, not across the cohort.
